name: Iwami Ginzan Silver Mine and its Cultural Landscape
description: Tucked into forested mountains in Shimane Prefecture, on the southwest coast of Honshu, Iwami Ginzan was Japan's largest silver mine, worked from 1526 until 1923. Visitors can walk into hand-cut tunnels, follow old trails down to the coast, and explore preserved mining settlements and port towns. Silver from here was shipped to Korea and China, and it helped drive Japan's economy in the 16th and 17th centuries.
